title: Moving math into methods
summary: DriveMath: numbers in, a number out.

say.never: A **method** is a named job. This one is called `linearSpeed`. You hand it two numbers (the left and right speeds), it does a little math, and it hands back one answer. `return` is how it hands the answer back.
say.bit: A method names a job. This one takes two numbers and returns their average.

say.never: These math methods live in a file called `DriveMath` and never touch a motor. That makes each one easy to check on its own, and it makes the robot code read almost like English: "give me the linear speed".
say.bit: `DriveMath` never touches a motor or sensor, so each method can be tested on its own. The drivetrain calls them, and `Robot.java` reads almost like a sentence.

say.never: Hold down **Ctrl** and tap **P**. A small search box pops up at the top. Type `DriveMath`, then press **Enter**. It finds any file by its name, so you never have to dig through folders.
say.bit: Press **Ctrl+P**, type `DriveMath` and press Enter. Quick Open finds any file by name, so you never have to dig through folders.
